# Data analysis: NMES1988

The `NMES1988` data (Deb and Trivedi, 1997; Zeileis, Kleiber, and Jackman,
2008), in the **AER** package, record the number of physician office visits
(`visits`) in 1987–88 for 4,406 people aged 66 and over in the US National
Medical Expenditure Survey. The covariates are the number of hospital stays
(`hospital`), self-perceived health (`health`: poor, average, excellent),
the number of chronic conditions (`chronic`), `gender`, years of education
(`school`), and whether the person has private insurance (`insurance`).

## Descriptive summary

```{r}
#| label: tbl-nmes-describe
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of the number of physician office visits."
y <- NMES1988$visits
desc <- c(n = length(y), mean = mean(y), variance = var(y),
          `variance / mean` = var(y) / mean(y),
          `observed zeros` = sum(y == 0),
          `Poisson expected zeros` = length(y) * dpois(0, mean(y)))
knitr::kable(t(desc), digits = 2, booktabs = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-nmes-hist
#| fig-cap: "Observed frequencies of physician office visits (bars; 30 = 30 or more) and frequencies expected under a Poisson distribution with the same mean (points)."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4
tab <- table(factor(pmin(y, 30), levels = 0:30))
bp <- barplot(tab, col = "grey80", border = "grey40",
              ylim = c(0, max(tab) * 1.1),
              xlab = "Physician office visits (30 = 30 or more)",
              ylab = "Frequency")
points(bp, length(y) * dpois(0:30, mean(y)), pch = 19, col = "firebrick")
legend("topright", c("Observed", "Poisson expected"), pch = c(22, 19),
       pt.bg = c("grey80", NA), pt.cex = c(2, 1),
       col = c("grey40", "firebrick"), bty = "n")
```

<!-- TO WRITE (you): what the table and figure show about overdispersion
and zeros. -->

## Model fitting

The Poisson model is fitted with `glm()` for reference; the NB and ZINB
models are fitted with this package. The count model uses `hospital`,
`health`, `chronic`, `gender`, `school`, and `insurance`; the zero-inflation
model uses `hospital`, `chronic`, `gender`, `school`, and `insurance`.

```{r}
#| label: nmes-fit
f_count <- visits ~ hospital + health + chronic + gender + school + insurance
f_zinb <- visits ~ hospital + health + chronic + gender + school + insurance |
  hospital + chronic + gender + school + insurance

m_pois <- glm(f_count, family = poisson, data = NMES1988)
m_nb   <- nbreg(f_count, data = NMES1988)
m_zinb <- zinbreg(f_zinb, data = NMES1988)
```

```{r}
#| label: nmes-zinb-summary
summary(m_zinb)
```

## Model comparison

```{r}
#| label: tbl-nmes-compare
#| tbl-cap: "Model comparison for NMES1988 (observed zeros = 683)."
pi_hat <- predict(m_zinb, type = "zero")
mu_hat <- predict(m_zinb, type = "count")
exp_zero <- c(
  Poisson = sum(dpois(0, fitted(m_pois))),
  NB      = sum(dnbinom(0, size = m_nb$theta, mu = fitted(m_nb))),
  # ZINB: P(Y = 0) = pi + (1 - pi) f_NB(0; mu, theta)
  ZINB    = sum(pi_hat + (1 - pi_hat) *
                  dnbinom(0, size = m_zinb$theta, mu = mu_hat)))
fits <- list(Poisson = m_pois, NB = m_nb, ZINB = m_zinb)
cmp <- data.frame(
  Model = names(fits),
  df = sapply(fits, function(m) attr(logLik(m), "df")),
  logLik = sapply(fits, function(m) as.numeric(logLik(m))),
  AIC = sapply(fits, AIC),
  BIC = sapply(fits, BIC),
  `Expected zeros` = exp_zero,
  check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(cmp, digits = 1, row.names = FALSE, booktabs = TRUE)
```

expected vs observed zeros for each model). -->

## Interpretation

```{r}
#| label: interp-helpers
# Exponentiated estimate with 95% Wald interval: exp(est +/- 1.96 SE)
wald_ci <- function(tab) {
  est <- tab[, "Estimate"]
  se <- tab[, "Std. Error"]
  sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", exp(est), exp(est - 1.96 * se),
          exp(est + 1.96 * se))
}
s_nb <- summary(m_nb)$coefficients[-1, ]
s_zc <- summary(m_zinb)$coefficients$count
s_zc <- s_zc[!(rownames(s_zc) %in% c("(Intercept)", "Log(theta)")), ]
s_zz <- summary(m_zinb)$coefficients$zero[-1, ]
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-nmes-irr
#| tbl-cap: "Count part: incidence rate ratios (IRR) with 95% Wald confidence intervals."
knitr::kable(data.frame(Covariate = rownames(s_nb),
                        `NB IRR (95% CI)` = wald_ci(s_nb),
                        `ZINB count IRR (95% CI)` = wald_ci(s_zc),
                        check.names = FALSE),
             row.names = FALSE, booktabs = TRUE, align = "lcc")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-nmes-or
#| tbl-cap: "ZINB zero part: odds ratios (OR) of being a structural zero, with 95% Wald confidence intervals."
knitr::kable(data.frame(Covariate = rownames(s_zz),
                        `OR (95% CI)` = wald_ci(s_zz),
                        `p-value` = format.pval(s_zz[, "Pr(>|z|)"], digits = 2),
                        check.names = FALSE),
             row.names = FALSE, booktabs = TRUE, align = "lcc")
```
